name: Union Square Ventures
history: Union Square Ventures was founded in New York in 2003 by Fred Wilson and Brad Burnham and closed its first fund, USV 2004, at $125 million. A thesis-driven early-stage firm from the start, it led or joined the first institutional rounds of Etsy (2006), Twitter (2007), Tumblr (2007), Zynga (2008), 10gen/MongoDB (2008), Kickstarter (2009), Twilio (2009), Duolingo (2011) and Coinbase (2013), added an Opportunity Fund for later rounds in 2010 (Cloudflare's $50M Series C, Lending Club, Stash, Justworks), and became one of the earliest institutional crypto investors (Coinbase, Protocol Labs, Algorand, Uniswap, Polygon). Since 2021 a parallel Climate fund family backs energy and carbon companies alongside the core Seed-and-A funds; the 2022 and 2024 core funds are $275 million each. The firm operates as one desk from Broadway in Manhattan under the partners Albert Wenger, Andy Weissman, Rebecca Kaden, Nick Grossman and Michael Mignano with the founders still listed, and reports as an exempt reporting adviser (CRD 162375) with 26 funds carrying $3.24 billion of gross assets at the March-2026 ADV. Its 220-company confirmed base spans 2004 to 2026 and reads seed-and-Series-A heavy, with 24 companies at $1B+ including five public floats above $10 billion.
investment_concept: USV invests at the edge of large markets being transformed by technological and societal pressures.
